## Problem

You are given an array of user identifiers. Write a function that produces a set of **random** pairings from this list, subject to the condition that every possible complete pairing configuration is equally likely. The process must obey the following rules:

- Two distinct users are selected at random to form a pair, and this continues until fewer than two users remain.
- The selection procedure must be uniformly random: each valid collection of pairs that could be generated from the input must have the same probability of occurring.
- When the input contains an odd number of users, exactly one user will be left without a partner.

**Example 1:**
> **Input:** ["Mike", "Sarah", "David", "Emma", "Alex"]
> **Output:** [["Sarah", "Emma"], ["Mike", "Alex"]]
**Explanation:** One possible outcome is [["Sarah", "Emma"], ["Mike", "Alex"]]. Because the total count is odd, "David" remains unpaired.

**Example 2:**
> **Input:** ["Jason", "Sophia", "Ryan", "Olivia", "Chris", "Megan"]
> **Output:** [["Jason", "Megan"], ["Ryan", "Chris"], ["Sophia", "Olivia"]]

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think about generating a random permutation of the users and then pairing them in order, which ensures all possible pairings are equally likely.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use the Fisher-Yates shuffle to randomize the order of the array, then pair consecutive elements (0-1, 2-3, etc.).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The complexity is O(N) time and O(1) extra space if you shuffle in place, watch for handling an odd number of users (one left unpaired).

</details>
